sections.text:
تستخدم هذه الطريقة لتقدير قوة العزل الكهربى للسوائل العازلة باستخدام العديد 
 من الأجهزة 
 الخاصة بهذا القياس التى تحقق المواصفه القياسية 
 IEC 156 
 ومن اهم عوامل نجاح هذا الاختبار الالتزام التام بخطوات تشغيل الأجهزة 
 والطرق القياسية المناسبة.

قام بإعداد هذا المستند 
 الكيميائي/ اشرف صلاح الدين صالح وتم مراجعة المستند 
 بمعرفة الكيميائي/
 عبد الناصر محمد الامين محمود 
 وقام بالاختبار السيد المشرف 
 الفنى/ 
 جمعة عبد الباسط عبد السلام وتم اعتماده من الكيميائى/ 
 محمد وجدى عبد الله 
 مدير عام بمحطة كهرباء السد العالى بشركة 
 المحطات المائية لإنتاج الكهرباء وموثق من المهندس/ 
 عبد النبى عبد الغنى عبد النبى 
 رئيس قطاع المحطة بشركة 
 المحطات المائية 
 لإنتاج الكهرباء.

وهذا المستند معتمد من المهندس/ 
 محمد اسامة سليمان سليم منسق الـMPIS بشركة 
 المحطات المائية لإنتاج الكهرباء.

rows:
قياس قوة العزل للسوائل العازلة يعطى دلالة هامة على 
 مدى تلوث الزيت بالرطوبة او الشوائب ولو بكميات صغيرة مما تؤثر سلبا على 
 قدرة الزيت كمادة عازلة.

يتم رفع الجهد على عينة الزيت بمعدل رفع منتظم حتى يحدث 
 الكسر فى الزيت ويتم تسجيل القراءة فى كل مرة ثم يؤخذ متوسط القراءات ويكون 
 قيمة جهد الكسر الناتج (الكيلوفولت) هو مقدار الجهد الذى يتحملة الزيت.
هو اقصى جهد (ك.ف) يتحمله الزيت كمادة عازلة عند اختباره.

قوة العزل (جهد 
 الكسر)

يتم اخذ العينة بالطريقة السليمة السالف ذكرها طبقا للـ 
 (MPIS(Oil-013-r2.

تأكد من صحة البيانات الواردة 
 على العينة.

التأكد من وضع 
 العينة فى الصندوق الخاص بها لعدم تعرضها لضوء الشمس والاتربة .
التأكد من ان زجاجة العينة جافة (خالية من المياه والاتربة).

عندعدم استخدام 
 الجهاز يتم حفظ الخلية والالكترود بوضع زيت صالح للاستعمال به ويتم وضعها 
 فى مكانها بالجهاز بعيدا عن الاتربة والغبار.
عند اجراء الاختبار نتجنب انسكاب الزيت على الارض وان حدث ذلك يتم ازالته.

يتوفر بالمعامل الاجهزة الموضحة والمستخدمة لاختبار 
 العزل الكهربى وتحقق المواصفات القياسية 
 IEC156 
 وهى
 جهاز الـ 
 Foster 
 واقصى مدى يصل اليه الجهاز 90 ك.ف 
 جهاز الـ Pgo 
 S3 
 واقصى مدى يصل اليه الجهاز 75 ك.ف 
 جهاز الـ T&R 
 واقصى مدى يصل اليه الجهاز 60 ك.ف

يتم استخراج خلية 
 الاختبار من داخل الجهاز ويفرغ الزيت الذى بداخلها ويجب التأكد من ان 
 المسافة بين قطبى الاكترود = 2.5 مم باستخدام المقياس الخاص بذلك.

تغسل خلية الاختبار بالزيت المراد اختباره اكثر من مرة 
 لضمان نظافة الخلية من اى شوائب.

قم بقلب زجاجة العينة المراد اختبارها بلطف عدة مرات 
 حتى يكون تجانس فى عينة الزيت ودون ان يسبب ذلك تكون اية فقاعات هواء.

تملأ خلية الاختبار بالعينة المطلوب اختبارها ببطء 
 لتفادى تكون فقاعات هواء على ان يكون الالكترود افل سطح الزيت بمسافة 4 سم 
 ثم تجفف الخلية من الخارج.

ضع خلية الاختبار فى المكان المخصص بالجهاز واغلق باب 
 الجهاز.

تأكد من توصيل الارضى بالجهاز ثم قم بتوصيلة بمصدر 
 التيار الكهربى واضغط على مفتاح التشغيل ليقوم الجهاز بعملية 
 العزل اتوماتيكيا طبقا 
 للمواصفة IEC 156 
 للحصول على عدد (6) قراءات يكون المتوسط لها هو اقصى جهد يتحملة الزيت 
 المختبر.

 spherical electrodes

sections_en.text: This method is used to determine the dielectric strength of insulating liquids using several apparatus for this measurement that comply with standard IEC 156. One of the most important factors for the success of this test is strict adherence to the operating steps of the apparatus and the appropriate standard methods.

This document was prepared by the chemist Ashraf Salah El-Din Saleh, reviewed by the chemist Abdel Nasser Mohamed El-Amin Mahmoud, tested by the technical supervisor Gomaa Abdel Baset Abdel Salam, and approved by the chemist Mohamed Wagdy Abdallah, General Manager of High Dam Power Station, Hydro Power Plants Company for Electricity Production, and certified by Eng. Abdel Nabi Abdel Ghany Abdel Nabi, Head of the Station Sector, Hydro Power Plants Company for Electricity Production.
This document is approved by Eng. Mohamed Osama Soliman Selim, MPIS Coordinator, Hydro Power Plants Company for Electricity Production.

rows: Measuring the dielectric strength of insulating liquids gives an important indication of the extent of oil contamination with moisture or impurities, even in small quantities, which adversely affects the ability of the oil as an insulating material.

The voltage is raised on the oil sample at a uniform rate until breakdown occurs in the oil; the reading is recorded each time, then the average of the readings is taken, and the resulting breakdown voltage (in kilovolts) is the voltage the oil can withstand.
It is the maximum voltage (kV) the oil can withstand as an insulating material when tested.
Dielectric strength (breakdown voltage)
The sample is taken in the correct manner mentioned above, in accordance with MPIS (Oil-013-r2).
Make sure the data on the sample are correct.
Make sure the sample is placed in its own box so that it is not exposed to sunlight and dust.
Make sure the sample bottle is dry (free of water and dust).
When the apparatus is not in use, the cell and electrode are stored with usable oil in them, placed in their place in the apparatus, away from dust and dirt.
When carrying out the test, avoid spilling oil on the floor; if this happens, remove it.

The laboratory has the apparatus shown, used for testing dielectric strength and complying with standard IEC 156, namely: the Foster apparatus, with a maximum range of 90 kV; the Pgo S3 apparatus, with a maximum range of 75 kV; and the T&R apparatus, with a maximum range of 60 kV.
Remove the test cell from inside the apparatus and empty the oil inside it; make sure the distance between the two electrode poles is 2.5 mm, using the gauge provided for that purpose.
Wash the test cell with the oil to be tested more than once to ensure the cell is clean of any impurities.
Invert the sample bottle to be tested gently several times until the oil sample is homogeneous, without causing any air bubbles to form.
Fill the test cell with the sample to be tested slowly to avoid air bubbles forming, so that the electrode is 4 cm below the oil surface, then dry the cell from the outside.
Place the test cell in its place in the apparatus and close the apparatus door.

Make sure the earth is connected to the apparatus, then connect it to the electric power source and press the power switch so that the apparatus performs the insulation test automatically according to standard IEC 156, to obtain (6) readings whose average is the maximum voltage the tested oil can withstand.

Introduction
This method is used to determine the dielectric strength of insulating liquids using several apparatus for this measurement that comply with standard IEC 156. One of the most important factors for the success of this test is strict adherence to the operating steps of the apparatus and the appropriate standard methods.
This document was prepared by the chemist Ashraf Salah El-Din Saleh, reviewed by the chemist Abdel Nasser Mohamed El-Amin Mahmoud, tested by the technical supervisor Gomaa Abdel Baset Abdel Salam, and approved by the chemist Mohamed Wagdy Abdallah, General Manager of High Dam Power Station, Hydro Power Plants Company for Electricity Production, and certified by Eng. Abdel Nabi Abdel Ghany Abdel Nabi, Head of the Station Sector, Hydro Power Plants Company for Electricity Production.
This document is approved by Eng. Mohamed Osama Soliman Selim, MPIS Coordinator, Hydro Power Plants Company for Electricity Production.
Objective
Measuring the dielectric strength of insulating liquids gives an important indication of the extent of oil contamination with moisture or impurities, even in small quantities, which adversely affects the ability of the oil as an insulating material. | 1.
Measurement Theory
The voltage is raised on the oil sample at a uniform rate until breakdown occurs in the oil; the reading is recorded each time, then the average of the readings is taken, and the resulting breakdown voltage (in kilovolts) is the voltage the oil can withstand.
Definition
It is the maximum voltage (kV) the oil can withstand as an insulating material when tested. | Dielectric strength (breakdown voltage)
Procedures Required for Measurement Accuracy
The sample is taken in the correct manner mentioned above, in accordance with MPIS (Oil-013-r2). | 
Make sure the data on the sample are correct. | 
Make sure the sample is placed in its own box so that it is not exposed to sunlight and dust. | 
Make sure the sample bottle is dry (free of water and dust). | 
When the apparatus is not in use, the cell and electrode are stored with usable oil in them, placed in their place in the apparatus, away from dust and dirt. | 
Environmental Recommendations
When carrying out the test, avoid spilling oil on the floor; if this happens, remove it. | 1.
Tools and Equipment Used
The laboratory has the apparatus shown, used for testing dielectric strength and complying with standard IEC 156, namely: the Foster apparatus, with a maximum range of 90 kV; the Pgo S3 apparatus, with a maximum range of 75 kV; and the T&R apparatus, with a maximum range of 60 kV. | 1.
Procedures to be Carried Out
Test Steps
Remove the test cell from inside the apparatus and empty the oil inside it; make sure the distance between the two electrode poles is 2.5 mm, using the gauge provided for that purpose. | 1.
Wash the test cell with the oil to be tested more than once to ensure the cell is clean of any impurities. | 2.
Invert the sample bottle to be tested gently several times until the oil sample is homogeneous, without causing any air bubbles to form. | 3.
Fill the test cell with the sample to be tested slowly to avoid air bubbles forming, so that the electrode is 4 cm below the oil surface, then dry the cell from the outside. | 4.
Place the test cell in its place in the apparatus and close the apparatus door. | 5.
Make sure the earth is connected to the apparatus, then connect it to the electric power source and press the power switch so that the apparatus performs the insulation test automatically according to standard IEC 156, to obtain (6) readings whose average is the maximum voltage the tested oil can withstand. | 6.
